learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will master advanced verb tenses, understand the sequence of tenses, and accurately apply narrative tenses in complex writing.]
warm_up_hook: ⏳ Time travel isn't just for science fiction! Tenses let you teleport your reader to the past, ground them in the present, or blast them into the future with just a few verb shifts. Let's start the time machine! 🚀

lesson_modules.module_title: 🕰️ The Present: Facts, Habits, and Ongoing Actions
lesson_modules.teaching_content: The Present tense is split into Simple (facts/habits), Continuous (actions happening right now), Perfect (past actions with present results), and Perfect Continuous (actions started in the past and still ongoing).
examples_or_templates: Simple: The committee meets every Friday. (Routine)
Perfect: She has written three novels so far. (Completed before now, relevance remains)

lesson_modules.teaching_content: When telling a story, we mix past tenses. Past Simple drives the main events, Past Continuous sets the background scene, and Past Perfect acts as the 'past before the past' to show the order of events.
examples_or_templates: Continuous & Simple: While we were sleeping (background), the alarm went off (interruption).
Perfect: By the time the police arrived, the thief had already escaped. (Earlier action)

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Future time is expressed using 'will' (spontaneous decisions/predictions), 'going to' (planned intentions/evidence-based predictions), or even present tenses for fixed schedules.
examples_or_templates: Going to: Look at those dark clouds; it is going to rain. (Evidence)
Present Simple for Future: The flight leaves at 8:00 AM tomorrow. (Schedule)

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Which tense correctly completes the sentence? 'I _____ on this project for three hours, and I am still not finished.'
❓ Identify the correct sentence showcasing the sequence of tenses:
options: He said that he will come tomorrow.
He said that he would come the next day.
He says that he would come the next day.
He said that he comes tomorrow.
practice_mcq_quiz.correct_answer: He said that he would come the next day.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fill in the blank with the appropriate past tense: 'When I got to the station, the train _____ (leave) already.'
subjective_practice.hint: Since the train left before you arrived, use the 'past before the past' (Past Perfect).

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Rewrite this sentence to express a scheduled future event using a present tense: 'The prime minister will arrive at 9 AM tomorrow.'
subjective_practice.hint: Use the Present Simple for fixed timetables and official schedules.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Spot the error and correct it: 'Since I moved to this city, I am visiting the museum three times.'
subjective_practice.hint: For actions that happened repeatedly from the past up to the present, use the Present Perfect.

activity_or_assignment.title: 📝 The Alibi Creator
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Imagine you are a detective interrogating a suspect. Write a short paragraph detailing what the suspect 'was doing', what they 'had done' earlier, and what they 'did' at the exact moment of the crime. Underline at least three different past tenses.

chapter_summary: ⭐ Present tenses handle routines, ongoing situations, and past actions with present consequences.
⭐ Narrative past tenses (Simple, Continuous, Perfect) are combined to show the exact timeline of a story.
⭐ Future time is flexible: use 'will' for spontaneity, 'going to' for plans, and present tenses for strict schedules.
